title: Computer Number Systems, Conversions & Data Representation

conversion_rules.method: Successive division by 2; record remainders in reverse order (bottom to top).
Multiply each binary digit by 2 raised to its positional power starting from right (2^0, 2^1, 2^2...) and sum up.
Group binary bits in sets of 3 from right to left; convert each 3-bit group to its octal equivalent.
Group binary bits in sets of 4 from right to left; convert each 4-bit nibble to hex (0-9, A-F).

complements.ones_complement: Invert all bits: 0 becomes 1 and 1 becomes 0.
complements.twos_complement: 1's Complement + 1. Standard method for representing signed negative integers in computer arithmetic.

coding_schemes.full_form: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
coding_schemes.facts: 7-bit code representing 128 characters (2^7 = 128, values 0 to 127). Extended ASCII uses 8 bits for 256 characters. Capital 'A' is 65 (01000001); lowercase 'a' is 97 (01100001); digit '0' is 48 (00110000).
Represents each decimal digit (0-9) using a 4-bit binary nibble (e.g. 25 in BCD is 0010 0101).

coding_schemes.full_form: Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code
coding_schemes.facts: 8-bit character encoding developed by IBM for mainframes.
Universal character encoding standard capable of encoding all world languages, mathematical symbols, and emojis (UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32). UTF-8 is the dominant encoding on the World Wide Web.
